author: Carol Yang
description:
Chinese archaeologists will carry out their first joint field project in South America by exploring sites dating back thousands of years in Peru as Beijing steps up its efforts to deepen cultural ties with the region.
The Institute of Archaeology of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences said it had signed a cooperation agreement with the Caral Archaeological Zone of the Peruvian Ministry of Culture and the Professional School of Archaeology at the National University of San Marcos to explore...
title: Chinese archaeologists heading to Peru for first joint project to explore ancient sites

author: Chao Kong
description:
Next time you spot a vivid orange-yellow crust spreading across a rock in your garden, on a country wall or along a hiking trail, take a closer look – you might be standing on a fortune.
A Chinese research team has found that a humble lichen could serve as a visible field indicator of unknown rare earth deposits around the world.
The researchers said the lichen’s distinctive colour made it easy to spot on exposed rock, and the discovery could be combined with unmanned aerial vehicles and...
title: Your backyard could hold a rare earth fortune – and this orange lichen is the clue

author: Victoria Bela
description:
China’s historic Chang’e-7 mission to drill for ice near the moon’s south pole has been delayed, the country’s human space flight programme authority said on Sunday.
The Chang’e-7 – carrying an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper – was expected to lift off aboard a Long March 5 rocket from the Wenchang spaceport in southern China’s Hainan province as early as Monday.
The China Manned Space Agency said on Sunday evening that the mission would be postponed following a comprehensive assessment...
title: China delays Chang’e-7 mission to drill for ice near lunar south pole

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
The United States may want the world to choose sides in the AI race with China, but in Africa, many businesses are pursuing a more pragmatic strategy: using Chinese models where they offer better value or flexibility, while keeping their options open.
For example, when African insurtech platform Curacel expanded the range of artificial intelligence (AI) models powering its internal infrastructure, it did not look only to Silicon Valley.
Instead, the Nigeria-based firm – which provides AI-powered...
title: The African firms adopting Chinese AI as US-China rivalry intensifies

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
The latest US artificial intelligence (AI) and supply chain initiatives are doomed to fail, according to a prominent political scientist who also argued that efforts to restrict US companies’ access to low-cost Chinese models would backfire.
Instead, he argued, the United States and China should collaborate on driving global economic development to generate the external demand needed to sustain long-term growth.
“US frameworks such as Pax Silica, the chip alliance and the rare earth alliance...
title: US efforts to secure AI supply chains are doomed to fail: Chinese academic

author: Orange Wang
description:
China has stepped up its offensive against a US-born school of thought on China’s last imperial dynasty, accusing it of providing “theoretical ammunition” for attempts to divide the country.
The denunciation comes as online debates over the Qing dynasty (1644-1911) continue to give rise to inflammatory rhetoric, and as Beijing’s ethnic policies and historical narratives are increasingly becoming an arena for international political competition.
An article published by the state-run China Ethnic...
title: Why Chinese media says US historians are giving ‘ammunition’ to separatists

author: Sylvia Ma
description:
The United States has pledged to take an “America First” approach to the latest round of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation talks, which are taking place in China weeks before President Xi Jinping’s visit to America.
The US State Department said: “US leadership in Apec is a key dimension to pursuing America First policies that foster prosperity and advance economic growth in the United States and across the region by breaking down barriers for US business, boosting fair and reciprocal trade and...
title: Washington pushes ‘America First’ agenda in Apec talks ahead of Chinese leader’s visit

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China’s secondary school students are dropping history as an exam subject, a trend that could leave the public more vulnerable to distorted narratives in the future, an academic at a top university has warned.
The note of caution comes as Beijing steps up efforts to counter “historical nihilism” – the official term for narratives that contradict or undermine the state’s official historical line – as well as pseudo-history, such as claims that Ancient Greece did not exist.
“History education in...
title: Gaokao reforms could leave Chinese public vulnerable to pseudo-history, top academic warns

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have created an AI-guided platform to engineer custom plant immune receptors to rapidly combat emerging diseases that threaten plants, including commercial crops vulnerable to devastating outbreaks.
Their programmable synthetic immune receptors can be introduced into plants to help them detect proteins made by specific bacteria, viruses and fungi, triggering an immune response to neutralise the threat, according to the team.
By leveraging protein design guided by artificial...
title: China builds world’s first custom plant immunity system for epidemic response
